# Future Directions — Snake-in-the-Box

This project formalises a chain of results about snakes (chordless induced
paths) in the hypercube `Q_n`, culminating in

* a proof of the **rigidity conjecture near the Boolean-cube ceiling**
  (direction 2 of the research programme), in a *strict* form, and
* the **exact optimum in dimensions two and three**, obtained from the same
  counting chain, and
* a **well-defined maximal snake length function** `maxLen n`, with a linear
  lower bound and the strict counting upper bound.

The statements live in two files, `Computation/SnakeInTheBox.lean` (steps 1–10)
and `Computation/SnakeMax.lean` (steps 11–15), which compile end-to-end with no
`sorry`, no `native_decide`, and no additional axioms (the main theorems depend
only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

## Setting

`Cube n = Fin n → Bool`, `Adj x y ↔ y` is `x` with one coordinate flipped, and

```lean
structure Snake (n L : ℕ) where
  v     : ℕ → Cube n
  step  : ∀ i, i < L → Adj (v i) (v (i + 1))
  chord : ∀ i j, j ≤ L → i + 2 ≤ j → 2 ≤ hammingDist (v i) (v j)
```

so `L` is the number of edges and `L + 1` the number of vertices.

## The chain, each link used by the next

1. **Cube basics.** `hammingDist_of_adj`, `adj_of_hammingDist`,
   `two_le_hammingDist_iff` (distance ≥ 2 ⇔ distinct and non-adjacent),
   `card_sphere` (the radius-one sphere has exactly `n` points).
2. **Snake basics.** `Snake.injOn` (vertices pairwise distinct),
   `Snake.card_vset` (`|S| = L+1`), `Snake.index_adj` (two snake vertices are
   cube-adjacent only if their indices are consecutive).
3. **Parity.** `par_flipAt`, `Snake.par_v` (parity alternates along a snake),
   `par_add_par` (parities sum to the Hamming distance mod two) and
   `Snake.three_le_hammingDist`: for indices of opposite parity that are at
   least two apart, the Hamming distance is at least **three** — a parity
   upgrade of chordlessness, the exact form of the "distance-two code on each
   parity class" phenomenon.
4. **Degree bound.** `Snake.degree_le_two`: chordlessness means each snake
   vertex has at most two of its `n` cube neighbours on the snake; hence
   `Snake.out_degree_ge`: at least `n − 2` edges leave the snake at each vertex.
5. **Double count.** `Snake.boundary_lower` (`(n−2)(L+1) ≤ ∂S`) and
   `Snake.boundary_upper` (`∂S ≤ n(2ⁿ − (L+1))`), combined in `Snake.count`:
   `(n−2)(L+1) + n(L+1) ≤ n·2ⁿ`.
6. **Rigidity.** `Snake.card_le`: for `n ≥ 3`, `L + 1 ≤ 3·2^(n−2)`;
   equivalently `Snake.omits` (a snake misses at least `2^(n−2)` cube vertices)
   and `Snake.not_hamiltonian` (no snake covers `Q_n`).
7. **Non-vacuity.** The explicit snake `000 → 001 → 011 → 111 → 110` of length
   four in `Q_3` (`snake3`), together with the dimension embedding
   `Snake.embed` (via `hammingDist_extend`, `adj_extend`), gives snakes of
   length four in every `Q_n`, `n ≥ 3` (`exists_snake_four`,
   `snake_length_bounds`).
8. **Exact endpoint degrees and the sharpened count.** The double count of
   step 5 throws away the fact that the two ends of the path have only one
   snake neighbour. `Snake.sum_vset` (sums over the vertex set are sums over
   the index range), `Snake.deg_split` (inside plus outside degree equals `n`),
   `Snake.nbrs_subset` and `Snake.degree_index_le` (the snake neighbours of
   `v i` lie in `{v (i−1), v (i+1)}`, minus the missing one at an endpoint) give
   `Snake.sum_degree_le`: the vertex set spans at most `L` cube edges. Feeding
   this into the boundary estimate yields `Snake.boundary_ge`
   (`n(L+1) ≤ ∂S + 2L`) and then

   > `Snake.count_sharp` :  `2n(L+1) ≤ n·2ⁿ + 2L`,

   i.e. `(2n−2)(L+1) + 2 ≤ n·2ⁿ`, a strict improvement on `Snake.count`.
9. **Strict rigidity.** `Snake.card_lt`: for `n ≥ 3`, `L + 1 < 3·2^(n−2)`, and
   `Snake.omits_lt`: a snake omits *more than* `2^(n−2)` vertices. This closes
   direction 2 of the programme with strict inequality.
10. **Exact optima in low dimensions.** Specialising `count_sharp` gives
    `Snake.length_le_dim_two` (`L ≤ 2` in `Q_2`) and
    `Snake.length_le_dim_three` (`L ≤ 4` in `Q_3`). With `Snake.truncate`
    (initial segments of snakes are snakes) and the explicit examples `snake2`,
    `snake3`, this becomes an exact characterisation:

    > `snake_max_dim_two`   : `Nonempty (Snake 2 L) ↔ L ≤ 2`
    > `snake_max_dim_three` : `Nonempty (Snake 3 L) ↔ L ≤ 4`

    So the longest snake in `Q_3` has exactly four edges — the classical value
    `s(3) = 4` — and the sharpened counting bound is *tight* in dimension three
    (it gives `L + 1 ≤ 5`, attained by `snake3`).

11. **Cardinality ceiling.** `two_le_hammingDist_of_two_ne` (two disagreeing
    coordinates force Hamming distance at least two) and `Snake.card_le_pow`
    (`L + 1 ≤ 2ⁿ`, from injectivity of the vertex sequence). The latter is
    what makes the set of achievable lengths bounded, hence step 14 possible.
12. **Extension by a fresh coordinate.** `Snake.lift` turns a snake of length
    `L` in `Q_n` into a snake of length `L + 1` in `Q_(n+1)`: embed the snake in
    the `xₙ = 0` layer and append the single flip of the new coordinate at the
    final vertex. Chordlessness of the new vertex is exactly step 11: it
    differs from every earlier vertex both in the fresh coordinate and (by
    `Snake.injOn`) in an old one.
13. **Linear lower bound.** Iterating step 12 from the seed `snake3` gives
    `exists_snake_dim : 3 ≤ n → Nonempty (Snake n (n + 1))`, so `s(n) ≥ n + 1`.
14. **The maximal length function.** `snakeLengths n = {L | Nonempty (Snake n L)}`
    is nonempty (`snakeZero`) and bounded (step 11), so
    `maxLen n = sSup (snakeLengths n)` is well defined and *attained*
    (`exists_snake_maxLen`, `maxLen_spec`). Combining the two halves of the
    chain:

    > `maxLen_lower`    : `3 ≤ n → n + 1 ≤ maxLen n`
    > `maxLen_upper`    : `3 ≤ n → maxLen n + 1 < 3·2^(n−2)`
    > `maxLen_succ_ge`  : `maxLen n + 1 ≤ maxLen (n+1)`
    > `maxLen_add_le`   : `maxLen n + k ≤ maxLen (n+k)`
    > `maxLen_mono`     : `maxLen` is monotone
    > `maxLen_two = 2`, `maxLen_three = 4`

    packaged as `maxLen_bounds`. `maxLen_add_le` is a weak additive shadow of
    the product conjecture (direction 4): the multiplicative statement would
    replace `maxLen n + k` by a product.

15. **Two extra edges per dimension.** `Snake.lift2` improves on `Snake.lift`
    by flipping the fresh coordinate at *both* ends: prepend the flip of `v 0`
    and append the flip of `v L`. The two new vertices share the value `1` in
    the fresh coordinate, so they are non-adjacent exactly because `v 0` and
    `v L` are (available as soon as `L ≥ 2`), and each is at distance at least
    two from every embedded vertex by `two_le_dist_extend_flip`. Hence
    `maxLen_succ_ge_two : 3 ≤ n → maxLen n + 2 ≤ maxLen (n+1)` and, by induction
    from `maxLen 3 = 4`,

    > `maxLen_lower_strong` : `3 ≤ n → 2n − 2 ≤ maxLen n`

    combined with the counting ceiling in `maxLen_final_bounds`:
    `2n − 2 ≤ maxLen n` and `maxLen n + 2 ≤ 3·2^(n−2)` for all `n ≥ 3`.

## Where the argument stops, and what to try next

* **Beating density `1/2`.** `count_sharp` gives `L + 1 ≤ (n·2ⁿ − 2)/(2n − 2)`,
  i.e. asymptotic density `1/2 + o(1)`; the records have density about `0.1` in
  dimension thirteen. The counting argument treats every vertex outside the
  snake as able to absorb `n` boundary edges. The first genuine saving would
  come from the vertices *outside* the snake with several snake neighbours:
  if `y ∉ S` is adjacent to `v_i` and `v_j` then `i` and `j` have the same
  parity and `|i − j| ≥ 2`, which is a strong local constraint that the present
  double count discards entirely. Formalising a weighted version of
  `Snake.boundary_upper` that reflects this is the natural next Lean step.
* **Parity-class packing.** `Snake.three_le_hammingDist` (already proved) says
  the odd-index/even-index cross distances are at least three. A Hamming-type
  sphere-packing statement for the pair of parity classes is the most promising
  route to a sub-`1/2` density bound, and the distance lemma it needs is in
  place.
* **Lower bounds (direction 1).** Steps 12–15 give the unconditional linear
  bound `maxLen n ≥ 2n − 2`, which is still very far from the conjectured
  `c·2ⁿ` (the true values are `4, 7, 13, 26, 50` for `n = 3, …, 7`). The
  gap is exactly the difference between adding *one* edge per new dimension and
  a *doubling* construction `s(n+1) ≥ 2s(n) − c` from reflected Gray-code-like
  concatenation. `Snake.lift` isolates the difficulty: after moving to the new
  layer one may not simply retrace the old path, because each new vertex
  `(v_i, 1)` is adjacent to the old `(v_i, 0)`. A doubling construction must
  therefore re-route inside the new layer, and the chord condition it has to
  maintain is precisely the parity-separated distance condition of step 3.
* **Products (direction 4).** With `Snake.embed`, `Snake.truncate` and the
  distance lemmas in place, the Cartesian product statement can be attacked by
  defining the candidate path on `Cube (m+n) ≃ Cube m × Cube n` and localising
  the offending chords at the interface steps.
* **Higher exact values.** The scheme of step 10 (counting bound plus an
  explicit optimal example) determines `s(n)` whenever the counting bound is
  tight. It is tight for `n = 2, 3` and fails from `n = 4` on
  (`count_sharp` gives `L ≤ 9` in `Q_4`, while `s(4) = 7`), so exact values in
  dimension four and above need either the local refinement above or a verified
  finite search.

## Honest status of the other conjectures

Directions 3 (completeness of the dimension-nine census) and 5 (sharp threshold
for greedy extension) remain out of reach of this formal development: the first
needs an enormous verified enumeration, the second a probabilistic model that
has not been formalised here. Direction 2 is now a theorem, in strict form.

# Future Directions

Concrete, falsifiable conjectures suggested by the formalisation in
`Catalog/Algebra/DerivedFunctors/`. Each one is stated so that a single Lean statement would
settle it, and each is a strict strengthening of something already proved in this project.

The formalised material (all of it complete, with no `sorry`, and depending only on the standard
axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`) is:

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `Resolutions.lean` | the short exact sequences `0 → ℤ --(·k)--> ℤ → ℤ/k → 0` and `0 → ℤ → ℚ → ℚ⧸ℤ → 0` |
| `ZModResolution.lean` | the bundled `ProjectiveResolution (ℤ/k)`; vanishing of `Lₙ₊₂F` on `ℤ/k`, in particular `Torₙ₊₂(G, ℤ/k) = 0` |
| `IntInjectiveResolution.lean` | the bundled `InjectiveResolution ℤ`; vanishing of `Rⁿ⁺²F` on `ℤ` |
| `LongExactSequence.lean` | the long exact (co)homology sequence of a short exact sequence of complexes, element-wise, plus consequences |
| `ExtZMod.lean` | `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≃ Y/kY`, via an explicit surjection `Y → Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y)` with kernel `kY` |
| `Ext.lean` | `Extⁿ⁺²(ℤ/k, Y) = 0`, `Extⁿ⁺²(X, ℤ) = 0`, `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) = 0 ↔ Y` is `k`-divisible, `Ext¹(ℤ/k, ℚ) = 0`, `Ext¹(ℤ/k, ℤ) ≠ 0` |
| `ExtFinitelyGenerated.lean` | vanishing of `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y)` whenever `X` has a projective presentation with projective kernel, freeness of the kernel of `ℤⁿ → X`, and `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0` for **every finitely generated** `ℤ`-module `X` |
| `Tor.lean` | `Tor₀ ≅ ⊗`, vanishing of higher `Tor` against flat modules, and the contrapositive |
| `FlatCriterion.lean` | `Flat ℤ G ↔ G` torsion-free `↔ ker(k·) = 0` for all `k ≠ 0` `↔ Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) = 0` for all `k ≠ 0` `↔ Torₙ₊₁(G, −) = 0`; `ℤ/k` is not flat for `k ≥ 2` |
| `UniversalCoefficients.lean` | universal coefficients with flat coefficients, and failure of exactness after tensoring with `ℤ/k` |
| `UCTTwoTerm.lean` | the universal coefficient isomorphisms `H₀(G ⊗ C) ≅ G ⊗ H₀(C)` and `H₁(G ⊗ C) ≅ Tor₁(G, H₀(C))` for the two-term free complex `C = (ℤ --(·k)--> ℤ)` |
| `TorZMod.lean` | `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]`, `G ⊗ ℤ/k ≅ G/kG`, `Tor₁(ℤ/k, ℤ/k) ≅ ℤ/k ≠ 0`, and the resulting non-exactness in degree one |

## C1. Naturality of the isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY`

The isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY` is natural in `Y`: for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ Y'` of
`ℤ`-modules the induced square, with vertical maps the isomorphisms and horizontal maps
`Ext¹(ℤ/k, f)` and the map induced by `f` on the quotients, commutes.

*Status.* The isomorphism itself is a theorem: `extOneZModEquiv` gives `Y ⧸ kY ≃+ Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y)`
for every `k ≠ 0`, built from the explicit surjection `y ↦ extClass ∘ (1 ↦ y)`
(`extOneHom_surjective`) whose kernel is exactly `kY` (`ker_extOneHom`). What is not formalised is
functoriality of this description in `Y`. Falsified by a morphism `f` for which the square fails
to commute.

## C2. Hereditarity of `ℤ`: all `Extⁿ` vanish for `n ≥ 2`

For all `ℤ`-modules `X`, `Y` and all `n : ℕ`, `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0`.

*Status.* Now proved in three cases. (i) `Extⁿ⁺²(X, ℤ) = 0` for all `X` (`ext_int_eq_zero`;
injective dimension of `ℤ` is `≤ 1`, and the bundled `intInjectiveResolution` gives `Rⁿ⁺²F(ℤ) = 0`
for every additive `F`). (ii) `Extⁿ⁺²(ℤ/k, Y) = 0` for all `Y` (`ext_zmod_eq_zero`). (iii) More
generally `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0` for every **finitely generated** `X` and every `Y`
(`ext_fg_eq_zero`), obtained from the free presentation `0 → ker f → ℤᵐ → X → 0` whose kernel is
again free (`free_ker_of_fin`) via the abstract criterion
`ext_eq_zero_of_projective_presentation`. The remaining case is `X` of infinite rank; it needs the
statement — not currently in Mathlib — that *every* submodule of a free `ℤ`-module is free.
Falsified by a single pair `X`, `Y` with `Ext²(X, Y) ≠ 0`.

## C3. `Tor₁` against the prime cyclic groups already detects flatness

For a `ℤ`-module `G`: `G` is flat if and only if `Tor₁(G, ℤ/p) = 0` for every **prime** `p`.

*Status.* The version quantified over all `k ≠ 0` is now a theorem:
`flat_iff_isZero_torOne_zmod` proves `Flat ℤ G ↔ ∀ k ≠ 0, Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) = 0`, via
`flat_iff_torsionFree` (flat = torsion-free over a Bezout domain),
`isZero_kernel_mulBy_iff` (`ker(k·) = 0` iff `k` acts injectively) and the computation
`torOneZModIso : Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]`; the strengthening
`flat_iff_isZero_tor_succ` shows flatness is equivalent to the vanishing of *all* `Torₙ₊₁(G, −)`.
The conjecture asks whether the test family can be shrunk to the primes, i.e. whether
`G[p] = 0` for all primes `p` forces `G[k] = 0` for all `k ≥ 1`. Falsified by a group `G` with
`G[p] = 0` for every prime `p` but `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≠ 0` for some `k`.

## C4. Balancing of `Tor`

For all `ℤ`-modules `G`, `H` and all `n`, the two left-derived functors of the tensor product
agree: `Tor(ModuleCat ℤ) n ≅ Tor'(ModuleCat ℤ) n`, and in particular
`Tor₁(G, H) ≅ Tor₁(H, G)`.

*Status.* Mathlib defines both `Tor` (derived in the second variable) and `Tor'` (derived in the
first) but does not prove them isomorphic. Our computation gives strong evidence in the cyclic
case: `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]` (`torOneZModIso`), which for `G = ℤ/m` has order `gcd(k, m)`,
symmetric in `k` and `m`; and `Torₙ₊₂(G, ℤ/k) = 0` (`isZero_Tor_two_le_zmod`) matches the
vanishing of `Tor'ₙ₊₂` predicted by the same resolution used in the other variable. Falsified by
a pair `G`, `H` and a degree `n` with `Torₙ(G, H) ≇ Tor'ₙ(G, H)`.

## C5. Universal coefficient theorem with the `Tor` correction term

Let `C` be a chain complex of free `ℤ`-modules and `G` an abelian group. Then for every `n` there
is a short exact sequence
`0 → Hₙ(C) ⊗ G → Hₙ(C ⊗ G) → Tor₁(Hₙ₋₁(C), G) → 0`,
natural in `C` and `G`, and split (non-naturally).

*Status.* We proved the theorem for the two-term free complex `C = (ℤ --(·k)--> ℤ)` in both
degrees: `H₀(G ⊗ C) ≅ G ⊗ H₀(C)` (`uctHomologyZeroIso`, no correction term since `H₋₁ = 0`) and
`H₁(G ⊗ C) ≅ Tor₁(G, H₀(C))` (`uctHomologyOneIso`, pure correction term since `H₁(C) = 0`,
`isZero_resComplex_homology_one`); the correction term is genuinely nonzero
(`not_isZero_uct_tor_term`, `torOneZMod_self_ne_zero`). We also proved the flat-coefficient case
`Hₙ(C ⊗ G) ≅ Hₙ(C) ⊗ G` for arbitrary complexes over any commutative ring
(`homologyTensorFlatIso`). Proving the general statement needs freeness of submodules of free
`ℤ`-modules (cf. C2) and the splitting `C ≅ Z ⊕ B[-1]`. Falsified by a free complex `C`, a group
`G` and a degree `n` where the displayed sequence is not exact.

# Future Directions

Status of the conjectures suggested by the formalisation in `Catalog/Bridges/`
(`OrdinalAnalysisBridge.lean`, `OrdinalAnalysisBridgeExtras.lean` and
`OrdinalAnalysisBridgeContinuity.lean`: the ordinal collapsing function `psi`, its term
rewriting system, and the order-preserving embedding of the `PA` notation system
`ONote`). Each item is stated so that it can be *refuted* by a single counterexample or
by a Lean proof of its negation.

Notation: `Ω = ω₁`; `Gen S` is the Skolem hull of `S ⊆ Ordinal` under `+` and `x ↦ ω^x`;
`gens a = {0, Ω} ∪ {psi c | c < a}`; `psi a = min (Gen (gens a))ᶜ`; `eps0 = ε₀`; `ε_ ·` is
Mathlib's `Ordinal.epsilon` (the enumeration of the fixed points of `x ↦ ω ^ x`).
Note that this `psi` uses the *unrestricted* hull: every `psi c` with `c < a` is a
generator at stage `a`, with no side condition `c ∈ Gen (gens a)`.

## Summary of what is now settled

All five original conjectures are settled: C1 is refuted, C2–C5 are proved. Beyond that,
`psi` is now completely determined:

| statement | Lean name |
| --- | --- |
| every value of `psi` is an epsilon number | `opow_psi` |
| `psi c = ε_c` for countable `c` | `psi_eq_epsilon_of_lt_Om` |
| `psi Ω = ε_{Ω+1}` | `psi_Om_eq`, `psi_Om_eq_epsilon` |
| `psi (Ω + a) = ε_{Ω+1+a}`, hence `psi a = ε_{Ω+1+(a−Ω)}` for `a ≥ Ω` | `psi_add_eq_epsilon`, `psi_of_Om_le` |
| `psi (Ω^ω) = ε_{Ω^ω}` and `bachmannHoward = ε_{ε_{Ω+1}}` | `psi_Om_opow_omega_eq_epsilon`, `bachmannHoward_eq_epsilon` |
| range of `psi` = all epsilon numbers except `Ω` | `range_psi` |
| above `Ω` the hull is the initial segment `Iio (psi a)` | `gen_iff_lt_psi` |

The headline chain of the first file, `ε₀ = ψ(0) < ψ(Ω^ω) ≤ ψ(ε_{Ω+1})`, and the bridge
theorems `ofONote_val_lt_psi_OmOmegaTerm`, `ofONote_val_lt_bachmannHoward` are unaffected
by all of this; in the new notation they read `ε_0 < ε_{Ω^ω} ≤ ε_{ε_{Ω+1}}`.

## C1. The collapse stays countable: `psi a < Ω` — **REFUTED (formally)**

Original conjecture: `∀ a, psi a < Om`. This is **false** for the unrestricted hull:
`Bridges.OrdinalCollapsing.not_forall_psi_lt_Om`. For `a < b` the ordinal `psi a` *is* a
generator at stage `b`, whereas `psi b ∉ Gen (gens b)`; so `psi a ≠ psi b`, and with
`psi_mono` this upgrades to `psi_strictMono`, hence `a ≤ psi a` (`self_le_psi`) and
`Om ≤ psi Om`. The exact form of the failure is now known: `psi c < Ω` *does* hold for
every countable `c` (`psi_lt_Om`), and the first value at or above `Ω` is
`psi Ω = ε_{Ω+1}`.

> **C1′.** Let `psi'` be the *restricted* Madore collapse, defined by
> `gens' a = {0, Ω} ∪ {psi' c | c < a ∧ c ∈ Gen (gens' a)}`. Then `psi' a < Ω` for every
> `a`, `psi'` is non-decreasing, and `psi' (ε_{Ω+1})` is the Bachmann–Howard ordinal.
> Falsifiable by exhibiting `a` with `psi' a ≥ Ω`. Formalising `psi'` requires a
> simultaneous recursion between the hull and the function, which is the main technical
> obstacle; the results proved here for `psi` (`psi_zero`, monotonicity, the bridge
> theorems) should transfer, since the two functions agree at `0` and the chain
> `ε₀ = psi 0 < psi (Ω^ω)` uses only generators of the form `psi c` with `c` explicitly
> in the hull.

## C2. Strict monotonicity of `psi` — **PROVED**

`psi_strictMono : StrictMono psi`, with `psi_ne_of_lt`, `self_le_psi`, `psi_unbounded`.
By C1 the strictness holds *globally* here rather than only below `ε_{Ω+1}`; for the
restricted collapse `psi'` of C1′ strictness below `ε_{Ω+1}` becomes a genuine open
problem again:

> **C2′.** `psi'` is strictly monotone on `Iio (ε_{Ω+1})` and constant on
> `Ici (ε_{Ω+1})`. Falsifiable by `a < b < ε_{Ω+1}` with `psi' a = psi' b`.

## C3. The rewriting system is confluent — **PROVED**

`Bridges.OrdinalAnalysis.step_confluent` and `step_church_rosser`, by the "canonical
form" route: an explicit normaliser `OTerm.norm` (flatten sums to the right via
`OTerm.appendT`, delete units) invariant under `Step` (`norm_eq_of_step`,
`norm_eq_of_rtstep`, `norm_eq_of_eqvGen`) and fixing normal forms (`norm_of_normal`),
whence unique normal forms (`normal_unique`, `norm_normal_form`).

> **C3′.** Extend `Step` by the Cantor-normal-form rules (ordering of summands,
> `ω^a + ω^b ⟶ ω^b` for `a < b`) and by `ψ`-specific rules; the extended system is still
> terminating and confluent, and its normal forms are in bijection with the ordinals
> below `psi (ε_{Ω+1})`. Falsifiable by a critical pair of the extended system that does
> not join, or by two distinct normal forms with the same value.

## C4. The image of the `Ω,ψ`-free fragment is exactly `Iio ε₀` — **PROVED**

`Bridges.OrdinalAnalysis.simple_val_range : {x | ∃ t, t.Simple ∧ t.val = x} = Iio eps0`,
via `simple_val_lt_eps0` and `exists_simple_of_lt_eps0`.

> **C4′.** The corresponding statement one level up: the values of terms using `Ω`, `+`
> and `ω ^ ·` but not `ψ` are exactly the ordinals below `ε_{Ω+1}` that are `Ω`-CNF
> representable, and the values of arbitrary terms are exactly the epsilon numbers
> reachable by `range_psi` together with their `Ω`-CNF combinations. Falsifiable by a
> `ψ`-free term whose value is not `Ω`-CNF representable.

## C5. Continuity at `Ω^ω` — **PROVED**

`psi_Om_opow_omega_eq_iSup : psi (Ω^ω) = ⨆ n : ℕ, psi (Ω^n)`, with
`psi_Om_pow_nat_lt` showing the approximations are strictly increasing. The proof is the
general continuity theorem `psi_of_limit`: for a limit `a > Ω` one has
`psi a = ⨆ c : Iio a, psi c`, because the supremum of the earlier collapses is itself an
epsilon number (`opow_psi`, `opow_iSup_psi_Iio`) strictly above every stage-`a`
generator, hence not generated.

Two findings refine the picture:

* the hypothesis `Ω < a` cannot be dropped: `psi_discontinuous_at_Om` shows
  `(⨆ c : Iio Ω, psi c) = Ω < psi Ω`, so `Ω` is the unique point of discontinuity;
* the value is explicit: `psi (Ω^ω) = ε_{Ω^ω}` (`psi_Om_opow_omega_eq_epsilon`).

> **C5′.** For the restricted collapse `psi'` of C1′ there is *no* analogue of the
> `Ω`-discontinuity: `psi'` is continuous at every limit `< ε_{Ω+1}`, i.e. it is a normal
> function on `Iio (ε_{Ω+1})`. Falsifiable by a limit `λ < ε_{Ω+1}` with
> `psi' λ ≠ ⨆ c < λ, psi' c`.

## New conjectures suggested by the closed form

> **C6.** *(Collapsing is exactly the loss of one epsilon number.)* For the unrestricted
> hull, `range psi = ε '' {a | a ≠ Ω}` is now a theorem (`range_psi`). Conjecture: for
> the restricted collapse of C1′, `range psi' = {ε_a | a < Ω} ∪ {ψ'-values below Ω}` is
> instead a set of order type `Ω` cofinal in `Ω`, and `psi'` is *not* injective.
> Falsifiable by proving `psi'` injective, or by exhibiting a value of `psi'` at or
> above `Ω`.

> **C7.** *(Notation systems.)* The term system `OTerm` modulo `Step` (equivalently, its
> normal forms) with the induced order is order-isomorphic to a *proper initial segment*
> of `Iio (psi (ε_{Ω+1}))`, not to all of it: the missing ordinals are exactly those
> whose `Ω`-CNF needs a value `psi a` with `a` not itself denoted by a term. Falsifiable
> by producing a surjection of term values onto `Iio (psi (ε_{Ω+1}))`.

> **C8.** *(Sharpness of the PA bridge.)* The `ψ`-free fragment of the term system and
> the `PA` notation system have the same values:
> `{t.val | t : OTerm, t.Simple} = {o.repr | o : ONote, o.NF}`, and `ofONote` maps every
> `NF` notation to a `Simple` term. Value preservation and order reflection are already
> proved (`val_ofONote`, `ofONote_val_lt_iff`, `strictMono_ofONote`), and the left-hand
> side is `Iio ε₀` (`simple_val_range`), so the conjecture is equivalent to: every
> ordinal below `ε₀` is `o.repr` for some `NF` notation `o`. Falsifiable by an ordinal
> `< ε₀` outside the image of `ONote.repr`, or by an `NF` notation whose `ofONote`
> translation is not `Simple`.

directions.description:
# Future directions

## What is in the repository

Three Lean files carry the mathematics of this mission (all of them compile and
contain no `sorry`):

* `Catalog/Bridges/GraphTheory/CayleyCharacterSpectra.lean` — the abelian, spectral
  story: characters as eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix
  (`adjMatrix_mulVec_char`, `adjMatrix_pow_mulVec_char`), the trace formula
  (`trace_pow_eq_charEigen_sum`), and the identification of the character power sum
  with `|G|` times a relation count
  (`charEigen_pow_sum_eq_card_mul_relationCount`,
  `closedWalk_count_eq_card_mul_relationCount`);
* `Catalog/Bridges/GraphTheory/CayleyWalkRelations.lean` — the counting half for *all*
  finite groups: for any base point, `#{closed k-walks at x} = #{(s₁,…,s_k) ∈ Sᵏ :
  s₁⋯s_k = 1}` (`card_closedWalk_eq_relationCount`), hence closed-walk counts are
  base-point independent (`card_closedWalk_eq_card_closedWalk`) and the total is
  `|G|` times the relation count;
* `Catalog/Novelty/LearningGraphicalSymmetries.lean` — the *local* translation
  invariance behind the census observables: explicit equivalences of neighbourhoods
  and of common neighbourhoods under left translation
  (`neighborEquivLeft`, `commonNeighborEquivLeft`), the pair-difference principle
  `commonNeighborEquivDifference` (the common neighbours of `(a,b)` are canonically
  equivalent to those of `(1, a⁻¹b)`), regularity (`degree_eq_identity`), the
  cardinality corollary `commonNeighbor_card_eq_difference`, and the fact that these
  equivalences preserve adjacency, so the *induced graph* on a common neighbourhood —
  not merely its size — depends only on `a⁻¹b`.

The first file builds a bridge between three descriptions of the same number, for a
finite abelian group `G` with a symmetric connection set `S` (`0 ∉ S`):

1. **Harmonic analysis** — the power sum `∑_{ψ ∈ Ĝ} (∑_{s ∈ S} ψ s)^k` over the
   Pontryagin dual;
2. **Spectral graph theory / linear algebra** — `trace(A^k)` for the adjacency matrix
   of the Cayley graph, i.e. the total number of closed `k`-walks;
3. **Additive combinatorics** — `|G|` times the number of length-`k` relations
   `s₁ + ⋯ + s_k = 0` inside `S`.

Natural continuations:

## 1. Nonabelian groups: spectral side
The counting statement is already proved for all finite groups in
`CayleyWalkRelations.lean`. What remains is the *spectral* half: replace characters by
irreducible representations, so that for `S` symmetric and conjugation-invariant the
adjacency operator acts on each isotypic component by the scalar `|S| χ(s)/χ(1)`, and
`trace(A^k) = ∑_χ χ(1) · (∑_{s∈S} χ(s)/χ(1))^k · χ(1)`. Combining that with the
relation count already proved would give the full nonabelian analogue of the bridge.

## 2. Cycle statistics in the census
For `k = 3, 4` the counts specialize to triangle and square statistics, the observables
whose empirical behaviour the source paper conjectures about. Deriving exact formulas
for the triangle count (`(1/6)(trace A³)` for simple graphs) and for square clustering
in terms of the additive structure of `S` would turn some of the paper's empirical
regularities into theorems, e.g.:
* `Cay(G,S)` is triangle-free iff `S` contains no solution of `s₁ + s₂ + s₃ = 0`
  (a sum-free-type condition);
* bipartiteness of `Cay(G,S)` iff there is no odd-length relation in `S`, which is
  equivalent to the existence of a character taking value `−1` on all of `S`.

## 3. Square clustering as a function on the group
`commonNeighbor_card_eq_difference` shows that the opposite-corner count entering the
square-clustering coefficient is a function `G → ℕ`, `g ↦ |N(1) ∩ N(g)|`, rather than a
function of ordered vertex pairs. Two concrete continuations:
* prove that this function is a *class function up to inversion*, i.e. invariant under
  `g ↦ g⁻¹` (using `x ↦ x⁻¹` on the connection set) and under automorphisms of `G`
  preserving `S`; this would explain the orbit structure visible in the census;
* express `|N(1) ∩ N(g)| = |S ∩ gS|` and derive the square-clustering coefficient as a
  normalized sum of these intersection numbers, giving a closed formula for abelian `G`
  via the character sums of `CayleyCharacterSpectra.lean`
  (`|S ∩ gS| = |G|⁻¹ ∑_ψ |∑_{s∈S} ψ s|² ψ(g)⁻¹`).

## 4. Spectral moments and eigenvalue distribution
`trace(A^k)` for all `k` determines the spectrum. The identity here therefore says that
the empirical spectral distribution of a Cayley graph is the pushforward of the uniform
measure on `Ĝ` by `ψ ↦ ∑_{s ∈ S} ψ s`. Making this precise (as a statement about
measures) and studying its limit for random `S` of fixed size as `|G| → ∞` (a
Kesten–McKay-type limit) is a well-posed next formalization target.

## 5. Expansion and diameter
The trivial character gives the top eigenvalue `|S|` (`charEigen_zero`). Bounding the
second eigenvalue `max_{ψ ≠ 0} |∑_{s∈S} ψ s|` yields expansion, hence diameter bounds
for the Cayley graph, connecting the census's distance statistics to character sums.
Formalizing the standard `diam ≤ O(log|G| / log(d/λ))` estimate in this setting is a
concrete goal.

## 6. Connectivity and generation
Complementary to the spectral side: `Cay(G,S)` is connected iff `S` generates `G`, and
the number of connected components is the index of `⟨S⟩`. Together with the OEIS
sequences of the source paper for groups generated by at most `k` elements, this gives
a formal statement of when the census's graphs are connected.

## 7. Beyond Cayley graphs
`Catalog/Novelty/UphoMultiplicability/Sabidussi.lean` characterizes Cayley graphs among
vertex-transitive graphs (Sabidussi). The boundary of the present results is exactly
this: a vertex-transitive graph still has orbit-invariant local statistics, but it need
not possess the canonical difference coordinate `a⁻¹b`, so
`commonNeighborEquivDifference` has no analogue. Making that failure precise — an
explicit vertex-transitive, non-Cayley graph (e.g. the Petersen graph) whose
common-neighbour profile is not a function of a single group element — would sharpen
the statement of what the Cayley hypothesis buys.

## Repository status

Every Lean file in `Catalog/` compiles under Lean 4.28 / Mathlib `v4.28.0` and the
whole package builds cleanly (`lake build` from the repository root). Completing that
build required repairing a number of previously truncated or unbuildable files; the
mathematically substantive repairs were:

* `Catalog/Shared/HilbertSpace/VectorStoneWeierstrass.lean` — the file had been left as
  a unified diff; the vector-valued Stone–Weierstrass development was reconstructed
  from it and now compiles;
* `Catalog/Shared/Hilbert6AxiomatizationofPhysics/SalvagedBest.lean` — the
  `EffectAlgebra` class and `EffectHom` structure were reconstructed from the surviving
  proof bodies, and cancellation, involutivity of the orthocomplement, transitivity and
  antitonicity of the natural order are proved from the axioms;
* `Catalog/Shared/BabelCodeasanovelmathematicalstructure/SalvagedBest.lean` — the
  missing `Volume`, `IsBabelCode`, `hammingBall` definitions and the column
  disagreement bound were supplied, so the Plotkin, Lawvere and sphere-packing bounds
  compile;
* `Catalog/Shared/BerggrenTrees/Parent_hyp_lt.lean` — the three inverse Barning–Hall
  parent maps and their positivity lemmas were reconstructed and proved;
* `Catalog/Algebra/Stoneweierstrasslattice/StoneWeierstrassLattice.lean` — an
  `axiom … : True` placeholder was replaced by the uniform-approximation form of the
  lattice Stone–Weierstrass theorem, proved from
  `ContinuousMap.sublattice_closure_eq_top`;
* `Catalog/Bridges/ProofTheoryAndLogic/AlgebraLogicBridge.lean` — the stated form of
  right distributivity for `Bool` is *false*; it is retained as a comment, refuted by
  `bool_right_distrib_counterexample`, and replaced by the correct law;
* `Catalog/Shared/CarmichaelComputational.lean` and its `NumberTheory` twin — the
  composite case of Carmichael's theorem is only certified for `n ≤ 10000`, so that
  hypothesis is now stated explicitly instead of being silently assumed.

Remaining frontier inside the catalogue: the unbounded (`n > 10000`) composite case of
Carmichael's primitive-divisor theorem, and the nonabelian spectral half described in
§1 above.

# Future Directions

Derived from the three files of this line of work:

* `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupCompleteInvariant.lean` (cycle 1) — connected groupoids
  (models of `K(G,1)`) are classified up to equivalence by the vertex group of a basepoint;
  a `π₁`-only counterexample shows the fundamental group alone does not classify.
* `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupK1Classification.lean` (cycle 2) — realization
  (`exists_functor_inducing`), homotopies are conjugations (`natIso_iff_conjugating_iso`,
  `realize_natIso_iff_conj`), the classification bijection `classificationEquiv`
  (`[K(G,1), K(H,1)] ≃ Hom(G,H)/conj`), Whitehead's theorem for 1-types
  (`isEquivalence_of_bijective_mapAut`) and its converse, sharpness
  (`connectedness_necessary`), and a counterexample where *all* positive-degree homotopy
  groups agree (`allHomotopyGroups_equiv_not_homotopyEquiv`).
* `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupK1Deepening.lean` (cycle 3) — see "Resolved" below.
* `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupPi0Gluing.lean`,
  `Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupPi0Decomposition.lean` (this cycle) — the coproduct of a
  family of groupoids is a groupoid (`sigmaGroupoid`), its `π₀` is the indexing set
  (`componentsSigmaEquiv`), equivalences glue over a bijection of indices
  (`sigmaEquivalence`), coproducts of connected groupoids are classified by index bijections
  matching vertex groups (`sigma_equivalence_iff`), every groupoid is equivalent to the
  coproduct of its components (`sigmaComponentsEquivalence`), and hence the pair
  (`π₀`, fundamental groups of the components) is a complete invariant of arbitrary homotopy
  1-types (`groupoid_equivalence_iff_pi0_aut`).  This resolves N2 below.

## Resolved since the last cycle

* **C1 (functoriality of the classification).**  `inducedHom_id` shows the identity functor
  induces the identity homomorphism, `inducedHom_comp_conj` shows the homomorphism induced by
  a composite is conjugate to the composite of the induced homomorphisms, and
  `toConjClass_comp` upgrades this to an exact identity of conjugacy classes.  So the
  classification bijection is compatible with composition; what remains open is the full
  2-categorical (bicategorical) statement, recorded as N1 below.
* **C3 (fibres of the classification).**  The conjugation action of `H` on `Hom(G,H)` has
  stabiliser exactly the centraliser of the image (`stabilizer_eq_centralizer`), so the set
  of homomorphisms realising a fixed homotopy class is a coset space of that centraliser
  (`orbitEquivQuotientCentralizer`) and has cardinality its index
  (`card_orbit_eq_index_centralizer`, `card_homs_natIso_realize`).
* **C2, discrete case.**  `π₀` is defined (`Components`), shown invariant under equivalence
  (`componentsEquivOfEquivalence`), trivial for connected 1-types
  (`subsingleton_components_of_connectedAt`), and shown to be a *complete* invariant of
  discrete (totally disconnected) 1-types:
  `discrete_equivalence_iff_nonempty_equiv : Nonempty (Discrete α ≌ Discrete β) ↔ Nonempty (α ≃ β)`.
  The general case (arbitrary groupoids) is restated as N2 below.

The following conjectures are concrete and falsifiable; each is stated so that a single Lean
counterexample would refute it.

## N1. The classification is a biequivalence, not just a compatible family of bijections

Conjecture: the assignment `(C, c) ↦ Aut c` extends to a biequivalence between the homotopy
2-category of connected groupoids with chosen basepoints and the 2-category whose objects are
groups, whose 1-cells are homomorphisms and whose 2-cells are conjugations.  Concretely, the
family of bijections `classificationEquiv` should be the hom-level part of a pseudofunctor:
there are coherent invertible comparison 2-cells for identities and composites (the conjugating
elements produced by `inducedHom_id` and `inducedHom_comp_conj`) satisfying the associativity
and unit coherence laws.  Falsified by exhibiting connected groupoids and functors whose
comparison conjugators cannot be chosen coherently.

## N2 (RESOLVED). `π₀` together with the vertex groups is a complete invariant of arbitrary 1-types

**Status: proved** — `FundamentalGroupPi0.groupoid_equivalence_iff_pi0_aut` in
`Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupPi0Decomposition.lean` states, for groupoids `C`, `D`:

```
Nonempty (C ≌ D) ↔ ∃ e : Components C ≃ Components D,
  ∀ p, Nonempty (Aut (Quotient.out p : C) ≃* Aut (Quotient.out (e p) : D))
```

The gluing step identified below as the content of the conjecture — every groupoid is
equivalent to the disjoint union of the connected full subcategories on its components — is
`sigmaComponentsEquivalence`; the coproduct half is `sigma_equivalence_iff` in
`Catalog/Bridges/FundamentalGroupPi0Gluing.lean`.  The original statement follows.

Conjecture: for arbitrary groupoids `C`, `D`, one has `C ≌ D` iff there is a bijection
`β : Components C ≃ Components D` together with, for each component, a group isomorphism of the
vertex groups of corresponding basepoints.  The `Discrete` case is now a theorem
(`discrete_equivalence_iff_nonempty_equiv`) and the connected case is cycle 2's
`connectedGroupoids_equivalent_iff_aut_mulEquiv`; the content of the conjecture is the gluing
step, i.e. that every groupoid is equivalent to the disjoint union (a `Sigma` of categories) of
the single-object groupoids of its components.  Falsified by two groupoids with matching
component data that are inequivalent.

## N3. The centraliser index is the exact size of every fibre, uniformly in the basepoint

Conjecture: for finite `H` the counting identity
`Nat.card {ψ // ψ conjugate to φ} = (Subgroup.centralizer (Set.range φ)).index`
proved as `card_homs_natIso_realize` refines to a *pointed* classification: pointed homotopy
classes of maps `(C, c) → (D, d₀)` (functors equipped with an isomorphism `F.obj c ≅ d₀`, up to
natural isomorphism respecting it) are in bijection with `Hom(Aut c, Aut d₀)` itself, and the
forgetful map to unpointed classes has fibre over `[φ]` of size `[H : C_H(φ(G))]`.  This is
falsifiable by a finite computation: take `G = H = S₃` (10 homomorphisms, 3 conjugacy classes,
orbit sizes 1, 3, 6, i.e. centraliser indices 1, 3, 6 — see `ComputationalEvidence.md`) and count pointed classes.

## N4. Asphericity is exactly the condition making `π₁` a complete invariant of maps

Conjecture: a path-connected space `X` is aspherical (a `K(G,1)`) **iff** for every
path-connected `Y` the map `[Y, X] → Hom(π₁ Y, π₁ X)/conj` is a bijection.  The "only if"
direction is the topological form of `realize_natIso_iff_conj`; the "if" direction should
follow by testing against `Y = Sⁿ`.  A formalisable first step, entirely inside the current
framework: prove that the fundamental groupoid functor `Top → Gpd` sends a map inducing an
isomorphism on `π₁` of path-connected spaces to an equivalence (a topological Whitehead
statement extending `fundamentalGroupoid_equivalence_of_mulEquiv` from existence of *some*
equivalence to the given map being one).

## N5. A genuinely higher counterexample

Conjecture: there exist path-connected `X`, `Y` with `π₁(X, x) ≃* π₁(Y, y)` that are not
homotopy equivalent — e.g. `S²` versus a point, distinguished by `π₂`.  The counterexamples
formalised so far (`same_fundamentalGroup_not_homotopyEquivalent`,
`allHomotopyGroups_equiv_not_homotopyEquiv`) are `π₀`-obstructions, which N2 explains
completely; a higher counterexample needs `π₂(S²) ≠ 0`, i.e. a degree or Hopf-invariant
argument that is not currently available in Mathlib.  Building that invariant is the concrete
task; the conjecture is falsified only if no such pair exists, which the informal theory rules
out, so the real content is the formalisation.

## N6. Homotopy classes of maps between *arbitrary* 1-types

The object-level classification is now complete for arbitrary 1-types
(`groupoid_equivalence_iff_pi0_aut`), while the classification of *maps* is so far only
available in the connected case (`classificationEquiv`).  Conjecture: for arbitrary
groupoids `C`, `D` with chosen component basepoints there is a bijection

```
Quotient (natIsoSetoid C D)  ≃  ∀ p : Components C, Σ q : Components D,
                                  Hom (Aut (rep p), Aut (rep q)) / conjugation
```

i.e. a homotopy class of maps of 1-types is exactly the data, for each component of the
source, of a target component together with a conjugacy class of homomorphisms of the
corresponding fundamental groups.  The ingredients are all in place:
`sigmaComponentsEquivalence` reduces both sides to coproducts, `Sigma.desc`/`Sigma.natIso`
decompose a functor and a natural isomorphism componentwise, and `classificationEquiv`
handles a single component.  It is falsified by a pair of groupoids for which the natural
comparison map fails to be injective or surjective; a finite search over groupoids with at
most two components and vertex groups of order at most 6 would already be decisive.

# Future directions

## State of the development

Every Lean file in the repository compiles end-to-end against Mathlib (`lake
build` from the repository root builds all declared libraries), and no file in
`Catalog/` contains a `sorry` or an `admit`.  The mission files use no axioms
beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.  See `BUILD_STATUS.md`
for the state of the unrelated `Shared/` scratch library, which was repaired as
part of this pass.  The mission files are:

* `Catalog/Cryptography/IsogenySIDH/KaniLemma.lean` — Kani's lemma in an
  abstract model of isogenies (abelian groups of points, group homomorphisms,
  dual isogenies given by their two degree relations, surjectivity of isogenies
  over an algebraically closed field), together with a concrete non-vacuity
  witness coming from complex multiplication by `ℤ[i]`.  The concrete side is
  now complete: the `n`-torsion of `ℚ/ℤ` is computed to have exactly `n`
  elements (`card_nTorsion_QZ`, via the exact sequence `0 → nℤ → ℤ → (ℚ/ℤ)[n]
  → 0` induced by `k ↦ k/n`), the `ℤ[i]`-action on `(ℚ/ℤ)²` is shown faithful
  (`gaussEnd_injective`), and consequently the Kani isogeny of the explicit
  `(5,2)`-diamond has kernel of order `N² = 49` (`cmDiamond_card_ker`).
* `Catalog/Cryptography/IsogenySIDH/RadicalMontgomery.lean` and
  `DeepRadicalMontgomery.lean` — correctness and exact fibers of the radical
  Montgomery `2`-isogeny formulas.

Natural continuations, roughly in order of increasing difficulty.

## 1. Replace the abstract model by Mathlib's elliptic curves

Mathlib has Weierstrass curves, their group law, and division polynomials, but
no theory of isogenies, dual isogenies, or degrees. The `Diamond` structure
used here isolates exactly the interface that such a theory must provide:

* `φ^ ∘ φ = [deg φ]` and `φ ∘ φ^ = [deg φ]`;
* surjectivity of a nonzero isogeny on geometric points.

Providing this interface for `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point` over an
algebraically closed field would immediately transport every theorem in this
file to genuine elliptic curves. The intermediate steps are: Vélu's formulas
for the quotient by a finite subgroup, multiplicativity of the degree, and
existence/uniqueness of the dual.

## 2. `#E[N] = N²` and the exact degree of the Kani isogeny

`card_ker_kani` reduces the degree computation `deg F = N²` to the statement
`#E₂[N] = N²`, i.e. `E[N] ≅ (ℤ/N)²` for `N` prime to the characteristic.  For
the CM torus this is now proved here (`card_nTorsion_QZ` together with
`card_nTorsion_prod` gives `#((ℚ/ℤ)²)[N] = N²`, whence `cmDiamond_card_ker`).
For genuine elliptic curves over a field the corresponding statement is a
classical result still absent from Mathlib; it would be a valuable standalone
addition (it also feeds the Weil pairing, already partially present in the
catalog).

## 3. The Castryck–Decru attack as an algorithm

The present file proves the *structural* half of the attack: the SIDH public
data determines a subgroup of `E₁ × E₄` which is exactly the kernel of an
`(N,N)`-isogeny of abelian surfaces (`mem_ker_kani_iff`), and this kernel is
the graph of an isomorphism `E₁[N] ≃ E₄[N]` (`exists_unique_partner_left` and
`glueMap_mem_ker`). Two further steps make it an algorithm:

* **Smoothness/decomposition.** When `N = 2^k` (or a product of small primes)
  the `(N,N)`-isogeny factors into `k` steps of `(2,2)`-isogenies, computable
  by Richelot's formulas. Formalizing Richelot correspondences on genus-2
  Jacobians is a substantial but self-contained project.
* **The splitting distinguisher.** The attack recovers the secret by testing
  whether the constructed abelian surface splits as a product of elliptic
  curves. `kani_ker_inter_left` and `kani_ker_inter_right` are the local
  statements behind this test; the global criterion needs the theory of
  principal polarizations and the Weil pairing on `E₁ × E₄`.

## 4. Isotropy of the kernel and the polarization

The kernel `{(φ^Q, ψ'Q)}` is isotropic for the product Weil pairing; this is
what makes `F` an isogeny of *principally polarized* abelian surfaces. With a
Weil pairing available (`Catalog/Cryptography/WeilPairingBLS.lean` has a start)
one can state and prove
`e_N(φ^Q, φ^Q') · e_N(ψ'Q, ψ'Q') = 1`, using `deg φ + deg ψ = N`.

## 5. The Deuring correspondence side

The mission statement also mentions the equivalence between computing an
isogeny from `j`-invariants and the quaternion isogeny path problem. A
formalization path: define the category of supersingular curves over `F_{p²}`
with its `ℓ`-isogeny graph, define maximal orders in `B_{p,∞}` with their
connecting ideals, and state the correspondence as an equivalence of groupoids.
Mathlib has quaternion algebras but no maximal-order theory, so this requires
building the arithmetic of quaternion orders first (norms, ideals, ideal
classes) — a large but very well-mapped project.

## 6. Generalizing the diamond

Kani's lemma holds for any commutative square with `deg φ = deg φ'`,
`deg ψ = deg ψ'`, not only for coprime degrees; only the *description* of the
kernel needs `gcd(a,b) = 1`. The computational evidence in
`ComputationalEvidence.md` shows that for `gcd(a,b) = d > 1` the kernel is
strictly larger than the graph. Determining the kernel in that case (it
contains `(E₁ × E₄)[d]`-type contributions) would be a natural refinement of
`mem_ker_kani_iff`.

# Future directions

## What is formalized

Four Lean files, all compiling with `lake build` and free of `sorry`:

* `Geometry/RomanDomination/Variants.lean` — the six Roman-type domination
  parameters (`γ`, `γ_R`, `γ_I`, `γ_dR`, `γ_p`, `u`), defined uniformly as
  infima of weights over classes of labellings, the full chain of comparison
  inequalities between them (`roman_chain`), and `γ_R(⊥) = n`.
* `Geometry/RomanDomination/ConvexBipartite.lean` — convex bipartite graphs
  (`IsConvexBipartite`), their `2`-colourability, convexity of `K_{m,n}`, and the
  exact values
  `γ_R(K_{m,n}) = min 4 (min (m+1) (n+1))` (`m, n ≥ 1`) and
  `γ_I(K_{m,n}) = min 4 (min m n)` (`m, n ≥ 2`).
* `Geometry/RomanDomination/DoubleRoman.lean` — the general bound `γ_dR(G) ≥ 3`
  for graphs with at least two vertices, and the exact double Roman domination
  number of `K_{m,n}` (`gammaDR_K_eq`): `3` if `min m n = 1`, `4` if
  `min m n = 2`, and `6` if `min m n ≥ 3` — the value `5` never occurs.
* `Geometry/RomanDomination/PerfectUnique.lean` — the exact perfect Roman
  domination number `γ_p(K_{m,n}) = min 4 (min (m+1) (n+1))`, which coincides
  with `γ_R(K_{m,n})`, and the exact unique response Roman domination number
  `u(K_{m,n}) = min (m+1) (n+1)`, together with the resulting unbounded gap
  `u - γ_p = min m n - 3` for `m, n ≥ 3`.

The key structural fact behind the unique response value is that in a complete
bipartite graph a vertex labelled `2` forbids *every* vertex on the opposite side
from carrying a positive label, so one side collapses to `0` and the other side
must avoid `0` entirely.

## Remaining directions

### 1. The interval structure of convex bipartite graphs

`IsConvexBipartite` is defined and `K_{m,n}` is shown to satisfy it.  The next
structural step is to extract, for a convex bipartite `G`, the two functions
`lo, hi : Fin n → ℕ` with `N(b) = [lo b, hi b]`, and to prove the monotonicity
lemma the left-to-right dynamic programming algorithms rely on: after processing
the first `k` left vertices, the only information about the past needed by the
future is which right vertices with `lo ≤ k` are still undominated.

### 2. Formalizing the dynamic programming algorithms

The eventual goal is a verified polynomial-time algorithm computing `γ_R`, `γ_I`,
`γ_dR`, `γ_p` and `u` on convex bipartite graphs.  A realistic decomposition:

1. define the DP state and the transition function as a Lean `def`;
2. prove *soundness* — every DP value is realised by some labelling;
3. prove *completeness* — every labelling is dominated by some DP run;
4. conclude that the DP optimum equals the `sInf` used in the definitions here.

Steps (2) and (3) are the mathematical content; the `sInf`-based definitions in
`Variants.lean` were chosen precisely so that such an equality is expressible
without any further glue.

### 3. Other structured graph families

`K_{m,n}` is the extreme convex bipartite graph.  Complete bipartite graphs minus
a perfect matching, bipartite paths and cycles, and stars with subdivided edges
are all convex bipartite and all have closed-form Roman-type parameters; each
would exercise the same lower-bound technique (a `0`-labelled vertex on one side
forces mass on the other side) already used here.

### 4. Chordal bipartite graphs and hardness

Chordal bipartiteness (every cycle of length at least six has a chord) is not yet
formalized here, because Mathlib's cycle API makes the "induced cycle"
formulation awkward.  A workable route is to define chordal bipartite via
*bisimplicial edge elimination orderings*, a purely finite combinatorial
statement equivalent to the cycle definition.  The NP-hardness side of the paper
would require a formal model of computation and polynomial-time reductions; this
is a much larger undertaking and is best kept separate.

### 5. Sharpness of the inequality chain

All the inequalities in `roman_chain` are known to be sharp.  Explicit witnessing
families make the chain a complete picture: `gammaR_bot` witnesses `γ_R = n`,
`gammaR_K` and `gammaDR_K_eq` witness `γ_dR = 3γ` for `K_{m,n}` with `m, n ≥ 3`,
and `gammaUR_sub_gammaPR_K` witnesses the unbounded `u`-versus-`γ_p` gap.  Stars
would give the remaining case `γ_R = 2γ`.

# Future directions

The new file `Catalog/Applications/SurveillanceNetworks/PrivacyThreshold.lean`
settles the "sharp privacy threshold" direction for binary network histories:
perfectly private channels — deterministic or randomized — achieve worst-case
Hamming distortion `D` exactly when a single ball of radius `D` covers the
history space, so the optimal private distortion is the covering radius of the
one-codeword code, and for binary tensors this is the full ambient dimension
`T·n²`. On the quantitative side the Hamming ball volume is computed exactly,
turning the fibre-covering converse into `2^{T n²} ≤ rate · ∑_{i ≤ D} C(T n², i)`,
with an excess-distortion version where only a good set of histories must be
reconstructed.

Open follow-ups:

1. **Entropy-sensitive converse.** Replace the counting version of the excess
   set by a probability measure: for a source law `p` on histories and a channel
   with excess-distortion probability `ε`, prove
   `H(X) - H(X | Y) ≥ H(X) - log(vol_D) - h(ε) - ε·log|S|` (Fano-type
   correction). The combinatorial skeleton (`card_good_le_rate_mul_ball`) is the
   counting shadow of this statement.

2. **Average- rather than worst-case distortion.** The threshold theorems here
   use almost-sure distortion. Under expected distortion a private channel can
   do better than the covering radius; identify the exact private
   rate–distortion function `D_priv(p) = min_c E_p[d(c, X)]` and compare it to
   the covering radius.

3. **Causal / sequential covering.** For time-indexed histories the record is
   produced online; replace the single covering number by a sequential covering
   number along the natural filtration and relate the resulting quantity to
   directed information.

4. **Structured sources.** For histories generated by a Markov chain on
   snapshots, the ambient count `2^{T n²}` is far from tight; a mixing-based
   deficit in the exponent is the natural next quantitative target.

5. **Distortion modulo relabeling.** Replace Hamming balls by orbit balls under
   the `S_n` action on vertices; the exact volume computation
   (`hamming_ball_card`) must be replaced by an orbit-counting (Burnside) volume,
   with graph asymmetry controlling the loss.

# Future directions

These conjectures are derived from the results proved this cycle in
`Catalog/Combinatorics/RamseyExponentialBounds.lean` (Part II of that file).
Each is stated so that a single Lean artifact settles it, and each comes with an
explicit falsification criterion.

Notation: `HasSubFourUpperBound r` means `∃ ε > 0, ∃ k₀, ∀ k ≥ k₀, r k ≤ (4-ε)^k`;
`HasProportionalSaving r` means `∃ q ∈ (0,1), ∃ k₀, ∀ k ≥ k₀, r k ≤ (4q)^k`.
Both are the catalog predicates from Part I, proved equivalent there.

## FD1. Subexponentiality is exactly the closure threshold for losses

Proved this cycle: every *subexponential* loss `L` (nonnegative, with
`∀ δ>0, L k ≤ exp(δk)` eventually) is absorbed by a proportional saving
(`hasSubFourUpperBound_of_subexponentialLoss`); and `L k = 2^k` is not
(`exponentialLoss_not_absorbable`, `not_subexponentialLoss_two_pow`).

**Conjecture.** Subexponentiality is *necessary*, not merely sufficient: for a
nonnegative `L`, the implication

> `(∃ k₀, ∀ k ≥ k₀, r k ≤ L k · (4q)^k)` for some `0 < q < 1` ⟹ `HasSubFourUpperBound r`

holds for **every** `r : ℕ → ℕ` if and only if `SubexponentialLoss L`.

*Falsified by:* a nonnegative `L` with `limsup (log L k)/k > 0` for which the
implication still holds for all `r`.  Such an `L` would have to hide its
exponential growth along a sparse subsequence, which suggests the correct
invariant is `limsup (log L k)/k` rather than the uniform bound we used.

## FD2. Root-test characterization

**Conjecture.** For every `r : ℕ → ℕ`,

> `HasSubFourUpperBound r ↔ limsup_{k→∞} (r k)^{1/k} < 4`.

This replaces the two catalog predicates by one analytic invariant, and would
re-derive `not_hasSubFourUpperBound_centralBinom` directly from
`C(2k,k)^{1/k} → 4`.

*Falsified by:* a sequence with `limsup (r k)^{1/k} = 4` that nonetheless
satisfies `r k ≤ (4-ε)^k` eventually, or a sequence with
`limsup (r k)^{1/k} < 4` and no such `ε`.

## FD3. Off-diagonal obstruction from the binomial bound

Proved this cycle (diagonal case): `¬ HasSubFourUpperBound Nat.centralBinom`,
i.e. the Erdős–Szekeres binomial estimate loses only a polynomial factor against
`4^k` and can therefore never produce an exponential saving.

**Conjecture.** The two-parameter analogue holds on every ratio window: for
`[a,b] ⊆ (0,1)`,

> `¬ HasProportionalSaving₂ (fun s t => (s+t).choose s) ramseyEntropyBase (ratioWindow a b)`.

Equivalently, `C(s+t,s)` matches `entropyBase(s/(s+t))^{s+t}` to within a
subexponential factor uniformly on the window.

*Falsified by:* an explicit `q < 1` and a window with
`C(s+t,s) ≤ (q · entropyBase(s/(s+t)))^{s+t}` for all pairs in the window.

## FD4. Effectivity of the threshold-elimination constant

Proved this cycle: `subFour_threshold_elimination` — an eventual sub-four bound
plus the strict small-case inequalities `r k < 4^k` gives one `ε > 0` valid for
all `k ≥ 2`.  The `ε` produced is a finite minimum of the individual gaps
`4 - (r k)^{1/k}` over `k ∈ [2,k₀)` together with the asymptotic `ε₁`.

**Conjecture.** For every `r` bounded above by the diagonal Ramsey numbers, the
binding constraint is asymptotic rather than small-case: the merged constant
equals `min(ε₁, 4 - (r 2)^{1/2})`, and in fact `4 - (r k)^{1/k}` is decreasing
in `k` on the known range.

*Falsified by:* an explicit `r` (e.g. the tabulated diagonal Ramsey numbers) and
an index `k` in the finite range whose individual gap is smaller than both `ε₁`
and the gap at `k = 2`.

## FD5. Necessity of the upper bound on the base in the two-parameter equivalence

Proved this cycle: if `m ≤ β ≤ M` on a parameter set with `m > 0`, then
`HasProportionalSaving₂ ↔ HasAdditiveGap₂` (`proportionalSaving₂_iff_additiveGap₂`);
for the entropy base the hypotheses hold with `m = 1`, `M = 2` on the *whole*
parameter set, so compactness of the ratio window is unnecessary
(`asymmetric_normalization_global`).

**Conjecture.** The upper bound `M` cannot be dropped in the general statement:
there exist `R : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ`, a base `β` with `1 ≤ β` but `β` unbounded above on
a set `S`, such that `HasAdditiveGap₂ R β S` holds while
`HasProportionalSaving₂ R β S` fails.

*Falsified by:* a proof of `HasAdditiveGap₂ → HasProportionalSaving₂` assuming
only a positive lower bound on `β`.

directions.description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Non-split Cartan curves and a characterization of fake elliptic curves' and formalize its key results. Abstract: The $\ell$-adic Tate module of an abelian surface with quaternionic multiplication (QM) decomposes as two copies of a two-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-rational representation. To this day, there is no criterion to distinguish these representations from those attached to elliptic curves. For this reason, QM abelian surfaces are usually called fake elliptic curves. In this paper we characterize QM abelian surfaces defined over an imaginary quadratic field $K$. Namely, we consider an abelian surface $A/K$ without potential CM and whose $L$-function is a square. Under a reasonable conjecture, we show that $A$ has QM if and only if it has residual image contained in a non-split Cartan group modulo at least two primes. The characterization is unconditional for all indefinite quaternion discriminants up to 33. The proof is based on previous work of Siksek and Michaud-Jacobs on quadratic points on non-split Cartan modular curves. In particular, we compute the rational points on the curve $X_{ns}^+
directions.proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.

directions.description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'On Diophantine equations over the integer rings of quadratic fields' and formalize its key results. Abstract: Let $K$ be any quadratic number field, and let $O_K$ be the ring of algebraic integers in $K$. In 1975 J. Denef proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over $O_K$ has a negative solution. In this paper we establish the following undecidability result: There is no algorithm to decide whether an arbitrarily given polynomial equation $P(z_1,\ldots,z_{16})=0$ (with integer coefficients and 16 unknowns) has solutions over $O_K$. Moreover, when $K$ is a real quadratic field, we show that $15$ unknowns suffice for undecidability.

# Future directions

## What is now proved in Lean (sorry-free)

All statements below are formalized and proved in this repository; every theorem checks with
only the standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

Notation: `n = |V(G)|`, `δ` = minimum degree, `κ` = vertex connectivity, `α` = independence
number, `τ` = toughness with the convention `τ(K_n) = ∞`.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/K2UnionK1FreeInvariants.lean`

* `k2UnionK1 k = K₂ ⊕g kK₁` and **`free_iff_isEmpty_embedding`**:
  `IsK2UnionK1Free G k ↔ IsEmpty (k2UnionK1 k ↪g G)`, i.e. the combinatorial definition from
  the earlier bridge file agrees with "no induced copy" in Mathlib's graph-embedding sense
  (milestone 1).
* A finite-graph invariant interface (milestone 2): `compCount G S` (components after
  deleting `S`), `ToughAtLeast G t` (`τ ≥ t`), `ToughGreaterThan G t` (`τ > t`),
  `IsHamiltonConnected`, together with `compCount_empty`, `two_le_compCount_of_isolated`,
  `compCount_compl_isIndepSet`, `ncard_neighborSet`, `two_le_compCount_neighborSet`.
* Toughness consequences (milestone 3): `connected_of_toughAtLeast`,
  `compCount_singleton_le_one` (no cut vertex), the separator inequalities
  `succ_compCount_le_ncard_of_toughGreaterThan_one`, `three_le_ncard_of_separator`, the
  degree bounds `two_le_minDegree_of_toughAtLeast`, `three_le_minDegree_of_toughGreaterThan_one`,
  and `two_mul_indepNum_lt`: `τ(G) > 1`, `n ≥ 3` imply `2α(G) < n`.
* Freeness × toughness: `two_mul_ncard_antiNeighborhood_lt`, `lt_two_mul_ncard_hasNeighbor`.
* Regression tests on `P₃`, `P₄`, `3K₁`.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/K2UnionK1FreeHierarchy.lean`

* `free_one_iff_edge_dominating`: `(K₂ ∪ K₁)`-freeness ⟺ every edge dominates every vertex.
* `hierarchy_strict`: the chain of classes is **strictly** increasing in `k`.
* `C₅` regression tests.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/K2UnionK1FreeToughnessBounds.lean` (new)

Every toughness inequality above is proved for an arbitrary rational parameter `t`, not just
`t = 1`.

* `compCount_le_one_of_ncard_lt_two_mul`: with `τ(G) ≥ t ≥ 0`, no vertex set of size smaller
  than `2t` disconnects `G`. With the predicate `VertexConnAtLeast G k` (`κ ≥ k`) this is
  `vertexConnAtLeast_of_toughAtLeast`, the classical bound **`κ(G) ≥ 2τ(G)`**;
  `connected_of_vertexConnAtLeast` and `VertexConnAtLeast.mono` complete that interface.
* `two_mul_lt_degree_of_toughGreaterThan`, `two_mul_le_degree_of_toughAtLeast`,
  `two_mul_lt_minDegree_of_toughGreaterThan`: `δ > 2t` when `τ > t` (and `δ ≥ 2t` when
  `τ ≥ t`) as soon as `n > 2t + 1`. The integral form is
  **`floor_two_mul_lt_minDegree`: `δ(G) ≥ ⌊2t⌋ + 1`** — this settles the previous cycle's
  Conjecture 5 affirmatively, with a weaker order hypothesis than conjectured.
* `succ_mul_ncard_isIndepSet_lt`, **`succ_mul_indepNum_lt`: `(t + 1)·α(G) < n`** whenever
  `τ(G) > t ≥ 0` and `n > t + 1`, generalizing `2α < n`.
* `succ_mul_ncard_antiNeighborhood_lt`, `lt_mul_ncard_hasNeighbor`: the same statements for
  the common antineighbourhood of an independent `k`-set in a `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free graph.
* `compCount_top_le_one`, `toughAtLeast_top`, `toughGreaterThan_top`: complete graphs satisfy
  every toughness predicate, confirming the convention `τ(K_n) = ∞`; plus regression tests
  (`K₅` is `4`-connected with `δ = 4`, `δ(C₅) = 2`).

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/K2UnionK1FreeParameter.lean` (new)

* **Heredity.** `IsK2UnionK1Free.of_embedding` (freeness transports along induced
  embeddings) and `IsK2UnionK1Free.induce`: the class is hereditary.
* **The freeness parameter.** `freeParam G = sInf {k | IsK2UnionK1Free G k}`, with
  `freeParam_spec`, the threshold property `freeParam_le_iff`, and monotonicity
  `freeParam_induce_le`, `freeParam_le_of_embedding`.
* **Bounds.** `free_indepNum` (every finite graph is `(K₂ ∪ α(G)K₁)`-free) gives
  **`freeParam G ≤ α(G)`**; `freeParam_eq_zero_iff` identifies parameter `0` with the
  edgeless graphs. Combined with the toughness bound: `succ_mul_freeParam_lt` and
  **`two_mul_freeParam_lt`: `2·freeParam(G) < n` whenever `τ(G) > 1`, `n ≥ 3`.**
* **Computed values.** `freeParam (cycleGraph 5) = 2`, `freeParam (k2UnionK1 k) = k + 1`,
  `freeParam ⊥ = 0`, `freeParam ⊤ = 1` for `n ≥ 2`.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/HamiltonConnectedDegree.lean` (new)

Necessary conditions for Hamilton-connectedness, the invariant counterpart of milestone 5.

* `two_le_degree_of_mem_support_of_ne`: a vertex interior to a path has two distinct
  neighbours (its predecessor and successor along the path).
* `two_le_degree_of_isHamiltonConnected`, `two_le_minDegree_of_isHamiltonConnected`:
  Hamilton-connected and `n ≥ 3` imply `δ ≥ 2`.
* **`three_le_degree_of_isHamiltonConnected`, `three_le_minDegree_of_isHamiltonConnected`:
  Hamilton-connected and `n ≥ 4` imply `δ ≥ 3`** — a degree-two vertex `v` with neighbours
  `a`, `b` would force the Hamiltonian `a`–`b` path to be exactly `a, v, b`.
* Obstructions `not_isHamiltonConnected_of_degree_lt_two`,
  `not_isHamiltonConnected_of_degree_lt_three`, applied to give
  `pathGraph_three_not_isHamiltonConnected` and `cycleGraph_five_not_isHamiltonConnected`;
  `isHamiltonConnected_bot_iff` checks the definition against the degenerate case.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/K2UnionK1FreeDiameter.lean` (new)

Metric consequences of the forbidden configuration.

* Distance-layer toolkit: `not_adj_of_dist_add_two_le` (vertices whose distances from a common
  base point differ by at least two are non-adjacent), `exists_dist_eq` (every intermediate
  distance is realised) and `exists_indepSet_dist` (the vertices at distances
  `a, a+2, …, a+2m` from `u` form an independent set of size `m + 1`).
* **`dist_le_two_mul_of_free`: a `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free graph has `diam(G) ≤ 2k` for `k ≥ 1`**
  (more precisely, any two vertices of one component are at distance at most `2k`), with the
  `ℕ∞`-form `ediam_le_two_mul_of_free`, the contrapositive `not_free_of_two_mul_lt_dist`, and
  the case `k = 1`, `dist_le_two_of_free_one`.
* **`dist_le_two_mul_freeParam`: `diam(G) ≤ 2·freeParam(G)`** for every connected finite
  graph, and the companion **`dist_lt_two_mul_indepNum`: `diam(G) < 2·α(G)`** proved by the
  same layer argument (a strengthening chain, since `freeParam ≤ α`).
* **Sharpness.** `pathGraph_free`: the path on `2k + 1` vertices *is* `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free (via
  the counting lemma `card_le_of_gap` for sets of naturals without two consecutive elements);
  `val_sub_le_walk_length` and `pathGraph_dist_ge` give the matching metric lower bound, and
  **`pathGraph_dist_eq`: the endpoints of `P_{2k+1}` are at distance exactly `2k`**, so the
  bound `2k` is attained for every `k ≥ 1`. On the other side, `pathGraph_not_free` and
  `lt_freeParam_pathGraph` show `P_{2k+2}` is not `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free.

### `Catalog/Combinatorics/LongestPathExchange.lean` (new)

The extension half of milestone 4, together with the step where freeness is used.

* `IsLongestPath p`: `p` is a path of maximum length among all paths of `G`;
  `exists_isLongestPath` (existence in a finite nonempty graph), `IsLongestPath.reverse`,
  `IsLongestPath.dist_le`.
* **`IsLongestPath.mem_support_of_adj_fst` / `mem_support_of_adj_snd`: every neighbour of an
  endpoint of a longest path lies on the path**, equivalently
  `IsLongestPath.not_adj_of_notMem_support`: the endpoints are anticomplete to the vertices
  the path misses.
* **`IsLongestPath.card_lt_of_indepSet_off`: the exchange step.** If the endpoints of a
  longest path are adjacent, then in a `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free graph every independent set of
  vertices missed by the path has fewer than `k` elements; `IsLongestPath.indepNum_off_lt`
  states this as `α(G − V(P)) < k`.
* `IsLongestPath.spanning_of_free_one`: for `k = 1` the missed set is empty, i.e. a longest
  path with adjacent endpoints in a `(K₂ ∪ K₁)`-free graph is Hamiltonian.


## Conjectures

Each is falsifiable by a single explicit finite graph (or by one exhaustive finite search).

**Conjecture 1 (small orders cannot separate `τ > 1` from Hamilton-connectedness).**
Every non-complete graph with `τ(G) > 1` and `n ≤ 9` is Hamilton-connected. *Evidence:*
exhaustively verified for `n ≤ 7` (§2 of `ComputationalEvidence.md`, an unverified external
enumeration); the Petersen graph (`n = 10`, `τ = 4/3`) is not Hamilton-connected, so the bound
`9` would be optimal. *Falsified by:* a graph on at most `9` vertices with `τ > 1` and two
vertices joined by no Hamiltonian path.

**Conjecture 2 (`k = 2` needs no degree hypothesis).**
Every `(K₂ ∪ 2K₁)`-free graph with `τ(G) > 1` and `n ≥ 3` is Hamilton-connected; in
particular the hypotheses `δ ≥ 2k` and `(k+1)`-connectivity of the headline theorem are
redundant when `k = 2`. Equivalently, in the language of the new invariant: `τ(G) > 1` and
`freeParam(G) ≤ 2` imply Hamilton-connectedness. *Evidence:* all non-complete graphs with
`τ > 1` on `≤ 7` vertices are Hamilton-connected, and every obstruction found so far has
`freeParam ≥ 3` (Petersen has `freeParam = 3`). *Falsified by:* a `(K₂ ∪ 2K₁)`-free graph with
`τ > 1` that is not Hamilton-connected.

**Conjecture 3 (the degree hypothesis `δ ≥ 2k` is far from optimal).**
For every `k ≥ 1`, every `(k+1)`-connected, `(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free graph with `τ(G) > 1` and
`δ(G) ≥ k + 1` is Hamilton-connected. *Evidence:* exhaustive check for `n ≤ 7`, no
counterexample; the Petersen graph has `k = 3`, `δ = 3 = k`, `κ = 3 = k`, so it violates both
weakened hypotheses and is consistent with the conjecture. *Falsified by:* a `(k+1)`-connected,
`(K₂ ∪ kK₁)`-free graph with `τ > 1`, `δ ≥ k + 1`, and a non-Hamilton-connected pair.

**Conjecture 4 (toughness improves the diameter bound to `freeParam + 1`).**
Every non-complete graph with `τ(G) > 1` satisfies `diam(G) ≤ freeParam(G) + 1`. *Evidence:*
`dist_le_two_mul_freeParam` proves the unconditional bound `diam ≤ 2·freeParam`, and every
example attaining it (the paths `P_{2k+1}` of `pathGraph_dist_eq`, and the stars) has
toughness at most `1`; the inequality `diam ≤ freeParam` itself is false (there are graphs of
order `5` with `τ = 3/2`, `diam = 2`, `freeParam = 1`), so `+1` is the right correction. An
exhaustive scan of all labelled graphs on `n ≤ 6` vertices and `4000` random graphs each on
`7` and `8` vertices produced no counterexample (external Python enumeration; see
`ComputationalEvidence.md`, not machine-verified). *Falsified by:* a non-complete graph with
`τ > 1` and two vertices at distance greater than `freeParam(G) + 1`.

**Conjecture 5 (the order bound `2·freeParam < n` is not tight).**
Every non-complete graph with `τ(G) > 1` satisfies `n ≥ 2·freeParam(G) + 2`. *Evidence:*
`two_mul_freeParam_lt` proves `n ≥ 2·freeParam + 1`; the parity-improved bound held in an
exhaustive scan for `n ≤ 6` and in random samples for `n = 7, 8, 9` (external Python
enumeration, not machine-verified), where the observed maxima were
`freeParam = 2` at `n = 6, 7` and `freeParam = 3` at `n = 8, 9`. *Falsified by:* a
non-complete graph with `τ > 1` and `n = 2·freeParam + 1`.

*(The previous cycle's Conjecture 5, `τ(G) > t ⟹ δ(G) ≥ ⌊2t⌋ + 1`, is no longer a conjecture:
it is proved as `floor_two_mul_lt_minDegree`. The two conjectures displaced from this list —
sharpness of `(t+1)α < n`, and Hamilton-connectedness above the threshold
`n ≥ 2·freeParam + 5` — remain open and untouched by the present cycle. A further
consequence of the new exchange step is worth recording as a target rather than a
conjecture: proving that in a `2`-connected graph some longest path has adjacent endpoints
would turn `IsLongestPath.card_lt_of_indepSet_off` into a bound on the vertices missed by a
longest path.)*

## Next formalization milestones

1. **Cycle rotation (the second half of milestone 4).** `LongestPathExchange` supplies the
   extension lemma and the freeness exchange step; what is missing is the rotation argument
   showing that in a `2`-connected graph a longest path can be closed into a cycle, after
   which `IsLongestPath.card_lt_of_indepSet_off` bounds the vertices off the path.
2. **Headline theorem (milestone 5).** The separator inequalities, `κ ≥ 2τ`, the degree
   bounds, the necessary condition `δ ≥ 3`, the diameter bound `diam ≤ 2k` and the exchange
   step are now available; the rotation argument of item 1 is the remaining gap.
3. **Toughness as a number.** Define `τ(G) : ℚ∞` and prove it agrees with the predicates
   `ToughAtLeast` / `ToughGreaterThan` (chosen here to avoid an `sInf` over an empty family
   for complete graphs), and likewise turn `VertexConnAtLeast` into a numerical `κ(G)`.
4. **Decidable regression harness.** Make `compCount`, `IsK2UnionK1Free` and `freeParam`
   decidable for `Fin n`-indexed graphs so that the finite checks in §2 of
   `ComputationalEvidence.md` — and the scans behind Conjectures 4 and 5 — can be replayed
   inside Lean by `decide` rather than by external enumeration.
